pairs.subject: fleet-orchestration
pairs.evidence: src/athena/daemon/tasks.py:422 a running task whose window died keeps its slot (and nothing ever marks it lost) until the window returns or the daemon restarts (ADR 0141 consequences, lines 112-113); companion_task has no last-heard-from column (tasks.py:120-135) and no sweeper, so each leaked slot permanently shrinks the cap of 3 and nothing bounds how long a dead task impersonates a working one.

techniques.evidence: src/athena/daemon/tasks.py:99 closed TASK_STATUSES vocabulary, id minted once at tasks.py:378, and every transition is a method on Tasks that rejects an illegal edge (finish only from running, tasks.py:497); the kill is final. Lineage and liveness fields are missing (see lifecycle-signals).

src/athena/daemon/tasks.py:422 the running count is the slot count and only finish, stop or the start-up sweep (tasks.py:524) lowers it; tier two (a staleness sweep with a per-state budget) does not exist, so a window that died mid-task leaves a ghost 'running' row and a held slot.

src/athena/daemon/server.py:1073 the start-up sweep marks every running row 'interrupted' (its own word, not 'failed') and tells the parent before the ready line, and every transition is committed in the row's write transaction before task.changed is published (tasks.py:439).

src/athena/daemon/tasks.py:385 the door holds two stock caps (3 running at tasks.py:422, 10 queued) and the queue is durable with identity kept at promotion (tasks.py:439) - but Athena authors her own next batch from each harvest line and no per-parent-conversation total is reserved at admission; ADR 0141 line 111 states 'the cap of 3 is the only cost control in v1'.
src/athena/daemon/tasks.py:560 every end (done, failed, killed, interrupted) is told to the parent thread as one episode, and failure is a first-class result with its own sentence (harvest_line).
src/athena/daemon/tasks.py:99 the status vocabulary has no hibernated state; a task is either queued, running or ended.

pairs.registryProposal: The map held not-applicable on a premise ADR 0141 removed (one turn at a time behind a writer lock). A daemon that admits a durable queue of delegated tasks with a running cap and a restart sweep is a small fleet; the golden path's precondition ('a set of autonomous sessions') holds from 2026-10-24. Upward lesson: lifecycle-signals could say what the minimum honest tier two is when the session's executor is another process the registry cannot probe (here the desktop window): a per-row last-turn timestamp and a staleness budget is cheaper than a process check.

pairs.subject: agent-runtime-assembly
pairs.evidence: src/athena/daemon/routes.py:906 _names_from reads the per-turn policy inputs (disabled_origins, gated_origins, gated_tools) from the request body and turns a missing or non-list value into an empty frozenset (line 907), so a malformed field re-enables switched-off apps and drops first-sight gating instead of failing the turn (guard-input-custody question 4: an absent policy input must fail loudly, not degrade to a permissive default).

techniques.evidence: src/athena/daemon/routes.py:906 absent or malformed policy input degrades to the permissive empty set; the oversize case does raise ListTooLong (line 909), so the loud path exists but the malformed path does not use it.

pairs.registryProposal: Re-anchored: the 2026-10-24 morning verdict cited routes.py:678 and 767-768, which the same day's fleet-surfaces commits moved (678 is now a closing paren); the finding is unchanged and now sits at routes.py:906-907. Note the docstring at routes.py:813-822 argues the opposite direction ('a malformed field must not switch an app on') but an empty disabled set is exactly the app-on state.
